req.title: load_logged_in_user populates g.user
req.statement: The system shall populate flask.g.user with the User row for the authenticated session on every request.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the system should populate flask.g.user with the User row for the authenticated session on every request. This behavior needs to be verified through positive, negative, and boundary test cases to ensure robustness and correctness of the implementation.

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_positive
preconditions: User Rahul is registered and logged in
actions: Make a request to the index page
expected: flask.g.user is populated with Rahul's user data
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Register and login user Rahul
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})

# Access the index page
r = client.get('/')

# Assert flask.g.user is populated
with app.test_request_context():
    assert g.user['username'] == 'Rahul'

# Assert HTTP 200 response
assert r.status_code == 200

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_boundary
preconditions: User Rahul is registered and logged in
actions: Make a request to the index page
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Register and login user Rahul
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})

# Clear the session
client.get('/auth/logout')

# Access the index page
r = client.get('/')

# Assert flask.g.user is None
with app.test_request_context():
    assert g.user is None

# Assert HTTP 200 response
assert r.status_code == 200
